- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.10) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.10) over 3–5 days, model overcorrects downward — adjust forecast upward to avoid excessive bearish bias.  
- Model often underestimates upward price spikes (especially after +0.30+ sentiment) — add 2–5% buffer to forecast for sudden rallies.  
- Model frequently overestimates downward moves after negative sentiment — reduce forecast by 1–3% if sentiment remains negative for 3+ days.  
- Forecast tends to lag true price by 1–3 days in upward moves — shift forecast 1–2 days ahead for momentum-driven rallies.  
- Mean reversion bias: if price is above 30-day moving average for 3+ days, reduce forecast slightly; if below, increase slightly — sentiment should guide direction.  
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overshoot early in the cycle — cap forecast at 1.5x recent 7-day high if sentiment is neutral or bullish.
